title: audit-vllm-kv-lifetimes
summary: Audit vLLM V1 asynchronous KV load/save completion, block retention, preemption, and receive-failure contracts when requests stall or blocks may be reused too early; requires a concrete connector trace.

skill_metadata.name: audit-vllm-kv-lifetimes
skill_metadata.description: Audit vLLM V1 asynchronous KV load/save completion, block retention, preemption, and receive-failure contracts when requests stall or blocks may be reused too early; requires a concrete connector trace.
limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.

applicability.scope: Pinned vLLM V1 scheduler/connector ownership audit for asynchronous KV load/save completion, retained blocks, preemption and failed receives; concrete connector conformance is not established by the interface.
applicability.prerequisites: A concrete connector and worker/model-runner call trace at identified revisions, with request/block events sufficient to compare actual callers against the pinned scheduler/interface contracts.
applicability.input_contract: Engine/connector revision and class, producer/consumer roles, KV-group count/block namespace, failure policy, concurrent-batch and graph modes; correlate bounded request IDs with allocation, matched tokens, load/save events, receive failures, preemption, finish and pool return.
applicability.produced_artifact: An ownership/event ledger and bounded contract-conformance report naming the earliest evidenced broken obligation, owner, affected requests/blocks and smallest missing observation, with a proposed targeted regression check.
applicability.failure_modes: Equating reserved tokens with usable KV, finished responses with reusable blocks, or send completion with scheduler write-fence completion can hide unsafe reuse; missing failed-receive completion can leave waits unreleased.
applicability.refusal_point: Escalate absent concrete caller evidence, ambiguous block namespaces, unsupported layouts or revision drift; stop before inferring a backend fix, freeing retained blocks or claiming a reproduced bug.

recommendations: Trace lookup, allocation, worker execution and completion propagation before changing request state; repeated or undecided lookup and ordinary admission waits can be valid.
Check delayed-free ownership and scheduler in-flight-write fences separately, including empty-step save/metadata ordering in the real worker.
Keep receive failure and finished_recving correlated, and use request-level failure evidence for multi-group layouts while preserving the existing recovery policy.
